question.problem:
Which of the following are elementary matrices?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ 3 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
An elementary matrix is a matrix obtained from the identity matrix by applying exactly one elementary row operation. 

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- The matrices $A$ and $C$ are not elementary matrices because they can't be obtained from ${I}_{2}$ by applying only one elementary row operation.

- The matrix $B$ is an elementary matrix because it can be obtained from ${I}_{2}$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}:=4{R}_{1},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{1}:=4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, only $B$ is an elementary matrix.
